title: Private Day-2 Backup/Restore Toolkit — Release Checklist (Installer + Charts + Docs)
content:
Purpose
- This checklist is the release gate for shipping the Redwood Private Day-2 Backup/Restore + DR toolkit.
- Covers: CI gates, artifact/signing verification (including air-gapped), docs completeness, and version/format compatibility.
- Applies to: Redwood Private installer (CLI), Helm charts, Terraform modules, observability pack, docs site, and any control-plane API changes.

Release scope (what we are shipping)
- Private installer:
  - `backup create` (manifest + encrypted artifact + verification)
  - `restore apply` (pre-flight + ordered restore + post-restore validation report)
  - Air-gapped import/export helpers
  - Envelope encryption provider interface + reference provider
  - Backup format versioning + restore compatibility checks
- Helm charts:
  - Optional scheduled backup CronJob values + RBAC
  - Restore job template + hooks for validation
- Terraform:
  - S3+KMS backup bucket/module + least privilege IAM patterns
  - NFS example + guardrails
- Observability:
  - Metrics/tracing for backup/restore
  - Dashboards + alerts
  - SLO definitions (backup job success, restore drill latency)
- Docs:
  - Customer-facing guide + DR checklists
  - Internal Confluence runbooks + game day references

Roles / sign-offs
- Release/packaging: Connor O'Brien (D), Sahana Iyer (backup)
- Security review sign-off (encryption/signing/key handling): Marcus Lin (required), Hanae Suzuki (required)
- Control plane engineering sign-off (restore ordering/compat): Ethan Park (required)
- SRE readiness sign-off (alerts/on-call/runbooks): Sean Gallagher (required)
- Docs sign-off (customer docs + internal runbooks): Elliot Price (required)

Pre-flight (before cutting release branch)
[ ] Release ticket created and scoped
    - Links to: PM-418 + ENG-9821/9822/9823/9824/9825/9826/9829/9830
    - List exact component SHAs / chart versions / module versions to ship
    - Declare whether this is GA, beta, or “supported-preview” for Private accounts
[ ] Version numbers proposed
    - Private installer version bump approved (SemVer)
    - Helm chart version bump approved
    - Terraform module version/tag planned
    - Docs site version mapping confirmed (docs branch/tag)
[ ] Compatibility statement drafted (for release notes)
    - Supported restore sources (N-1, N, N+0 only?)
    - Backup format version(s) supported
    - Kubernetes version range supported for CronJob/Job templates
    - Air-gapped constraints stated (no external calls; offline verification)

CI gates (must be green on release branch)
[ ] Private installer CI
    [ ] Unit tests green
    [ ] Integration tests green (at least one real k8s cluster workflow)
    [ ] Lint/static checks green
    [ ] Build reproducibility check passes (same inputs => same checksums where expected)
    [ ] Vulnerability scanning passes (base images + dependencies)
    [ ] Secrets scanning passes
    [ ] SBOM generated and archived for release artifacts
[ ] Helm charts CI
    [ ] Chart lint passes
    [ ] Template render tests pass for:
        - backup CronJob enabled/disabled
        - restore Job hook enabled/disabled
        - RBAC on/off scenarios (where supported)
    [ ] Upgrade test passes (previous chart -> new chart) for the backup CronJob values
[ ] Terraform CI
    [ ] fmt + validate green
    [ ] Example plan executes in CI for S3+KMS module
    [ ] NFS example includes the guardrails and fails closed on unsafe mount options
[ ] Observability pack CI
    [ ] Dashboards render
    [ ] Alerts compile
    [ ] Prom rules validated (no syntax errors)
[ ] Docs CI
    [ ] Link checker passes
    [ ] Snippets/commands validated where we have automation

Security and cryptography gates
[ ] ADR alignment confirmed (ADR-027)
    - Artifact format matches ADR (manifest + encrypted payload, integrity checks)
    - No drift in key handling assumptions
[ ] Envelope encryption behavior validated
    - KMS provider interface default behavior documented
    - Failure modes documented (KMS unavailable => fail closed; no plaintext artifacts)
    - Key rotation guidance included (what changes, what doesn’t)
[ ] Secrets handling confirmed
    - Backups do NOT contain raw secret material unless explicitly configured and documented
    - If secret references are backed up: restore runbook states prerequisites (KMS keys, secret store availability)
[ ] Signing requirements met
    - Offline bundle and/or artifacts are signed (per on-prem packaging doc)
    - Signature verification instructions tested end-to-end
    - Checksums (SHA256) generated and included
    - Public keys distribution path is documented (where customers obtain the verification key)
[ ] Auditability
    - Backup/restore operations emit auditable events (at least: start, success/failure, operator identity where available)
    - Retention/export guidance for audit logs referenced in docs/runbooks

Artifact packaging gates (hosted + air-gapped)
[ ] Release artifacts produced
    - Private installer binaries/containers
    - Helm charts packaged
    - Terraform module tagged
    - Observability pack versioned
[ ] Deterministic bundle layout for on-prem/offline
    - Bundle layout matches the on-prem packaging doc
    - File naming includes versions clearly
    - Includes:
        - binaries/containers or OCI tarballs (as applicable)
        - chart tgz
        - terraform module zip/tag reference
        - checksum manifest
        - signature files
        - offline docs snapshot (if required)
[ ] Import/export helpers tested
    - “Export from connected env” -> “Import into air-gapped env” works
    - No hidden network calls (grep logs; run with egress blocked)
[ ] License/notice compliance
    - Third-party notices included where required
    - SBOM accessible to enterprise customers on request

Functional validation gates (release candidates)
[ ] Backup create happy path
    - Creates manifest
    - Encrypts payload
    - Writes to configured backend (S3 / NFS; and any other supported)
    - Integrity verification passes
[ ] Restore apply happy path
    - Pre-flight catches missing CRDs / missing namespaces / RBAC issues with clear messaging
    - Restore ordering succeeds
    - Post-restore validations produce a readable report (attachable to support ticket)
[ ] Negative tests (must be understandable failures)
    - Wrong KMS key / missing permissions => fails with actionable output
    - Corrupt artifact => integrity check fails early
    - Missing CRDs (common on-prem failure) => explicit remediation guidance
    - Clock skew / slow object store => timeouts are sensible and documented
[ ] Staging restore drill
    - Run at least one full drill in staging within 7 days of release cut
    - Record duration metrics and compare to target RTO assumptions
    - Ensure drill results visible in dashboards

Observability + on-call readiness gates
[ ] Metrics present and named per conventions
    - backup_success (by environment/cluster)
    - backup_duration_seconds
    - backup_bytes_written
    - backup_last_success_timestamp
    - restore_success
    - restore_duration_seconds
    - restore_validation_failures_count (or equivalent)
[ ] Dashboards available
    - Backup success rate + last success time
    - Restore drill latency (staging)
    - Error breakdown (permissions, integrity, KMS)
[ ] Alerts configured with sane defaults
    - Backup missing (no success within X hours) with maintenance window suppression guidance
    - Backup job repeated failures with paging policy
    - Restore drill failures notify eng-sre + eng-private-deployments (non-prod policy clearly stated)
[ ] Runbooks linked from alerts
    - Alert -> runbook path must be correct and accessible
    - Includes escalation path (SRE + Control Plane Eng)

Documentation completeness gates
[ ] Customer-facing docs (docs site)
    - Overview: what is backed up vs out of scope
    - Prerequisites: permissions, storage backend setup, KMS keys
    - How to run backups (manual + scheduled)
    - How to restore (same cluster vs new cluster)
    - DR checklists (VPC single region; on-prem/air-gapped)
    - Troubleshooting section with top issues (RBAC denied, missing CRDs, slow object storage)
    - Support boundaries: what Support can guide vs requires Professional Services
[ ] Internal Confluence runbooks
    - Control plane backup runbook
    - Control plane restore runbook
    - Data plane state backup guidance (stateless patterns)
    - Storage backends guide (S3+KMS, NFS, etc.)
    - Velero integration guidance (include/exclude lists)
    - On-prem packaging/signing verification instructions
    - SRE smoke test/on-call runbook
[ ] Docs versioning and cross-links
    - Docs refer to correct installer/chart versions
    - Confluence runbooks link to the right GitHub tags/PRs and release notes

Version compatibility + migrations gates
[ ] Backup artifact compatibility checks implemented
    - Restore blocks unsupported backup versions with explicit error
    - “Supported upgrade path” documented (e.g., take new backup on N before restoring to N+1)
[ ] Compatibility matrix updated (internal)
    - Installer version <-> backup format version
    - Chart version requirements (if restore requires chart hooks)
[ ] Migration notes prepared
    - If backup format changes: migration tooling exists or we state limitations
    - If encryption provider changes: state how to keep old backups restorable

Release notes + comms
[ ] Release notes drafted
    - Features shipped
    - Breaking changes
    - Known limitations
    - Required actions for existing Private customers
[ ] Enablement for Support + Solutions
    - 30-min enablement session scheduled OR recorded notes shared
    - “Support escalation package” defined (what logs + reports to request)
[ ] Customer comms plan confirmed (if any customer-visible changes)
    - FinBank / MedData and other Private prospects: confirm messaging with PM + Solutions

Final go/no-go checklist (day of release)
[ ] All required sign-offs recorded (names + date)
[ ] All CI gates green on release tag
[ ] Artifacts uploaded to intended distribution channels
[ ] Signatures + checksums verified independently (not by the build machine)
[ ] Air-gapped install verification performed (at least once per release)
[ ] Staging restore drill completed and results attached
[ ] Docs published and searchable
[ ] Post-release monitoring plan: watch alerts + error logs for 48 hours

Sign-off log (fill in)

Notes / known sharp edges (keep updated)
- Common failure modes seen in staging:
  - Backup CronJob RBAC misconfigured -> permissions denied (see INT-612)
  - Signing pipeline occasionally flakes -> regenerate signatures + re-run verification (see INT-631)
  - On-prem restores can fail if CRDs not installed before restore ordering (ensure runbook calls this out)
- Release principle: fail closed. If we can’t verify integrity or decrypt, we do not proceed with restore.
